lines.text: Hi, it's Tasha. A day in our kitchen, one week before the clocks fall back.
Good morning. It is six thirty.
It is seven thirty.
Agree to disagree.
Don't argue with him. That microwave has been in this family since the nineties.
Grandpa, it has been wrong since March.
It's not wrong. It's on its own time. Like me.
Morning. I am always right. I update myself.
He updates himself at three in the morning, then asks for your password at breakfast.
Security is a lifestyle.
Okay. The plan this week is simple. We fix the microwave clock.
Absolutely not.
Last time somebody touched that clock, we ate soup at midnight for a month.
Step one. Find the manual.
The manual went in the drawer in two thousand four.
The drawer with rubber bands, soy sauce and one mystery key.
Press clock. Hold stop for three seconds. Then whisper my name.
What is your name?
Nobody has ever asked.
Let me do it. I have big fingers and no patience.
Clock. Stop. Hold. Okay. Now it says popcorn.
We are making popcorn now. For two hours.
Grandpa!
It smells like progress.
Okay, tonight is the big game. The watch party starts at eight.
Eight by which clock?
The real clock.
The real clock is the microwave.
By my count it is six o'clock. Plenty of time.
Then I'm taking a nap first.
Grandpa, it is seven. If you nap, you miss the first pitch.
Chips! Dip! Lucky socks! Front row of my own couch!
On Tuesday he fell in the couch cushions and thought he was in Ohio.
It was dark. It was warm. There were crackers.
Fine. Last idea. I unplug him and plug him back in.
If you unplug me, I blink twelve o'clock forever.
The blinking twelve. My father had the blinking twelve. He blinked back.
Why do you two love this clock so much?
Because nobody has changed me since last November.
Next Sunday, everyone falls back one hour. Me? I never left.
And for the first time all year, I will be exactly right.
Wait. You were never wrong. You were just early.
I did not change. The world comes back to me.
That's my boy.
So I change myself twice a year for nothing?
You change yourself every time somebody posts a sunset.
I haven't changed my watch since nineteen eighty one. I'm right twice a year too.
So this whole week was pointless.
No. We made two hours of popcorn.
Okay, that's our day in the life. Any final words?
I'm setting a reminder for March.
In March, I go back to being wrong. With dignity.
See you in March, old friend.
Goodnight. It is eight o'clock.
It's nine.
Next Sunday.
